environment.orchestrator: none required: the retained C1 compiler slice is a pure, in-memory, deterministic component with no external service dependency
environment.reused_deliverable: ocor_runtime.c1.ports (OCOR-DEV-0011, sealed and unmodified) supplies SourceUnit/CompilerRequest/DependencyLockEntry/CanonicalIrRelease/ArtifactManifestEntry, the C1Error/C1Diagnostic/DiagnosticCode fail-closed contract, and the generic verify_deterministic_build reproducibility oracle; this task adds only a real YAML/JSON parser, a semantic validator, and a canonical IR builder implementing those sealed Protocols

commands.command: full local pytest regression, ocor-runtime/tests/ (OCOR_LIVE_POSTGRES_DSN set locally, pointed at the ocor-bootstrap postgresql service)
full local pytest regression, 3 reports/tests suites

requirement_results.command: a versioned DSL fixture (mixed YAML and JSON sources) compiles to an immutable canonical IR release, including a migration-metadata artifact summarizing the release's resource/version identity, with a real SHA-256 ir_digest
verify_deterministic_build (sealed, OCOR-DEV-0011) proves two independent compilations of the identical request produce byte-identical canonical bytes, ir_digest and artifacts
an import reference absent from the dependency lock is rejected by the sealed CompilerRequest constructor itself, before the retained builder ever runs
genuinely malformed YAML (unterminated flow sequence) is rejected with a SOURCE_INVALID diagnostic, never silently parsed as something else

parsed content missing required keys, or whose 'fields' is not a mapping, is rejected with a TYPE_ERROR diagnostic; a declared id that does not match its own SourceUnit.resource_id is rejected with a CONSTRAINT_ERROR diagnostic
the negative acceptance criterion proven directly: a rejected compilation never returns any CanonicalIrRelease object, partial or otherwise
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: This is the smallest contract-compliant slice: RetainedOacParser/RetainedSemanticValidator/RetainedCanonicalIrBuilder implement OacParser/SemanticValidator/CanonicalIrBuilder only. IrSigner (real cryptographic signing), ReleasePublisher, SemanticDiffEngine, MigrationPlanner, ArtifactGenerator (beyond the one migration-metadata artifact), CompatibilityChecker and ConformanceSuitePort remain unimplemented Protocols in the sealed ports module, each its own future task.
signature_envelope_ref is an honestly-labeled unsigned placeholder (urn:ocor:unsigned:<core-digest>), not a real signature envelope; no signing claim is made or implied.

The DSL's minimal shape contract (a top-level 'id' plus a 'fields' mapping) is deliberately narrow, matching 'the smallest contract-compliant implementation'; it does not attempt to anticipate every future schema shape the real C1 ontology DSL will need.

canonical_digest (RFC 8785) requires I-JSON-safe values; a 'fields' mapping containing a non-JSON-safe YAML type (e.g. a date or a custom tag) would raise from the canonicalizer rather than from this module's own validation -- an honest current limitation, not a silently swallowed case.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: This component is pure and stateless (no durable side effects, no external service, no persisted state to roll back); a rollback is a plain revert of the isolated commit, mechanically reviewed rather than drilled, consistent with the task's own rollback_procedure for a component with no runtime state.
